draft.title: Prenatal development
card: Prenatal development is the growth that happens before birth. It begins at fertilisation, when a sperm joins an egg, and lasts about 40 weeks.
Germinal stage
the first two weeks or so. The fertilised egg divides into a ball of cells, travels to the uterus and attaches to its wall.
Embryonic stage
from about week 3 to week 8. The main organs and body systems begin to form, including the heart, brain and spinal cord.
Fetal stage
from about week 9 until birth. The organs mature and the body grows quickly, and the baby gains weight.
draft.remember: Prenatal development runs from fertilisation to birth in three stages: germinal, embryonic, fetal.

a.q: During which stage do the main organs and body systems first begin to form?
opts: Embryonic stage
Germinal stage
Fetal stage
Postnatal stage
a.why: The embryonic stage, from about week 3 to week 8, is when the heart, brain and spinal cord start to form. The germinal stage is tempting, but it is only the early cell division and attachment to the uterus wall.
a.clue: Organs start forming after the egg has attached to the uterus.

b.q: Priya is 14 weeks pregnant. Her baby's organs are already formed and are now maturing as the body grows. Which stage is the baby in, and why?
opts: Fetal, because it is after week 8 and organs are maturing
Embryonic, because the organs are still being formed
Germinal, because the cells are still dividing rapidly
Fetal, because it is before the baby's organs have formed
b.why: The fetal stage starts at about week 9, and its main task is maturing organs and growing. The embryonic stage is tempting because organs are mentioned, but that stage ends at about week 8 and Priya is at week 14.
b.clue: Compare week 14 with the week where the embryonic stage ends.

b.best: Fetal, because it is after week 8 and organs are maturing

problems.detail: The card says prenatal development 'begins at fertilisation' and 'lasts about 40 weeks'. The 40 weeks is counted from the last menstrual period. From fertilisation it is about 38 weeks. The stage weeks (3–8, 9 to birth) are counted from fertilisation, so the card mixes two counting systems. Say 'about 38 weeks from fertilisation (about 40 weeks of pregnancy)'.

The stem already says the organs 'are already formed and are now maturing'. That rules out the embryonic option and the 'before the organs have formed' option. The right option also repeats the stem's word 'maturing' and is the only one with a precise detail ('after week 8'). A student can match words instead of applying the stage timing.

b.q: Priya's baby was conceived 14 weeks ago. Which stage of prenatal development is the baby in, and why?
